(Editorial fiction) Two people have read the same batch of interviews, and the decision is the same one: whether a particular passage can serve as an example of "reasons for leaving". The material is the same, the permission is the same, and the privacy requirement is the same. One may focus on whether this quotation can carry the explanation running through several pieces, and whether the conclusion still stands without it; the other may focus on whether the person agreed to be quoted this way, and whether they would still be recognisable after the edit.

Both are shared checks: if the explanation does not hold, the quotation has no place; if permission is unclear, a complete explanation still cannot be used. Which of the two gets thought of first depends more on who knows the material, who spoke to the interviewee and who handles publication than on anyone's type. Either type could think of either item first on the same afternoon.

The workable move is to ask the two questions separately and let both answers change the plan: first "which pieces of evidence does this conclusion still need", then "has the person confirmed how far this material can be used". Once both have answers, decide how much to share.

(Editorial fiction) Hearing that a friend does not want to talk for now, either may start guessing why, and either may step back first. Two things can be checked: whether your reading of the situation is accurate, and whether the space the friend wants has been respected.

One may think the friend has been busy all week and wonder about setting a regular time to ask again; the other may think the friend has already declined once and want to offer care without creating an obligation to reply. Both worries fit into one sentence: "I will not push; I am here when you want to talk, and Friday works too if that helps." That states what support is available and hands the pace back.

If the friend never responds, there is no need to read the silence as a signal: leave one line saying no reply is needed and wait, or ask directly "what would help — do you want me to listen, or to take one concrete thing off your plate?" Help counts once the other person confirms it, and that has nothing to do with either type.

| Shared task | INFJ: what could be settled | INFP: what could stay open | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Date and venue while replies are pending | Confirm a slot so attendees can arrange travel. | Hold two available slots until the pending replies arrive. | J/P: when to confirm the date |
